body:
## Summary
Convert `bootstrap.sh` into an Ansible role (`roles/dotfiles/`) that replaces as much of it as possible — a holistic rewrite serving reliability/idempotency, maintainability, and multi-machine profiles. A thin residual `bootstrap.sh` (~30 lines) survives only to solve the chicken-and-egg of installing brew + ansible and then execs the playbook. Of the session-daemon `eval`s, `gpg-agent --daemon` and `mise activate` stay in shell-startup (`bash_profile`/`zshrc`), where they already run on every login. `ssh-agent` is **not** wired into shell startup today (see follow-up #155) — on macOS the keychain handles SSH auth; on Linux passphraseless keys work without an agent.

## Motivation / Context
The user's raw idea: "turn this dotfiles repo into an ansible role that replaces as much of the bootstrap.sh as possible."

`bootstrap.sh` is a 485-line bash script: symlinks, dir creation, terminfo, GPG/SSH key generation + agent setup, TPM plugin install, OS prereqs (apt/pacman), rustup, mise, a large Homebrew formulae/cask list, vim-plug + nvim plugins, pynvim/neovim gem/gopls, zoxide migration, beads hydration. Drivers: fix the idempotency bugs (#41 rm -rf no backup, #45 non-idempotent macOS SSH config, dedupe #48), replace 485 lines of bash with declarative YAML, and enable per-machine customization (overlaps with #152).

## Requirements

### Layout & invocation
- **Role-in-repo + local playbook.** Standard `roles/dotfiles/{tasks,defaults,handlers,files,templates,vars,meta}/` in this repo.
- Top-level `playbook.yml` targets `localhost` with `connection: local` (configured via `ansible.cfg` so no inventory file is needed for the common case: `ansible-playbook playbook.yml`).
- Dotfile files move into `roles/dotfiles/files/` and are symlinked into `$HOME` via the idempotent `ansible.builtin.file` module (`state: link`, `force: yes`) — replaces the `rm -f` + `ln -sf` pattern and **fixes #41** (the backup strategy becomes: Ansible's `force` overwrites non-links; pre-existing regular files are backed up via a `copy` task with remote suffix before linking).
- Reusable externally: `ansible-galaxy install git+https://github.com/tribou/dotfiles`.

### Scope (Aggressive — all but session-daemon evals)
Ansible performs everything except the session-daemon `eval`s that cannot mutate the parent shell from a subprocess. Of these, `gpg-agent --daemon` and `mise activate bash` come up via existing shell-startup wiring (`bash_profile`/`zshrc`) when the user opens a fresh login shell after the run. `ssh-agent` is **not** wired into shell startup today — it is out of scope here (tracked in a follow-up #155): on macOS the keychain handles SSH auth; on Linux passphraseless keys work without an agent. The role's `ssh` task does replicate the macOS `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain` keychain pre-load (a real persistent effect); the dead Linux inline `ssh-agent` subprocess eval is dropped as cleanup.

#### Task structure (tagged, by concern)
Tasks split into focused files under `roles/dotfiles/tasks/`, each tagged:

| Tag | File | Covers (current bootstrap.sh lines) |
|---|---|---|
| `dirs` | `dirs.yml` | `~/dev/bin`, `~/dev/go/{pkg,src/...}`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.config/{nvim,alacritty,mise}`, `~/.local/bin`, `~/.ssh`, `~/.tmux` (42-47, 87, 103, 108, 113, 122, 127) |
| `links` | `links.yml` | all symlinked dotfiles: `.bash_profile`, `.vimrc`←`init.vim`, `.gitconfig`, `.zshrc`, `.tmux.conf`←`tmux/tmux-conf`, mise default packages, `.gnupg/gpg-agent.conf`, nvim `init.vim`+`coc-settings.json`, alacritty, mise config, helper scripts (52-65, 69-74, 89, 105, 110, 115, 119, 123-124) |
| `terminfo` | `terminfo.yml` | `tic -x tmux/*.terminfo` via `command` with `changed_when` (83-84) |
| `gpg` | `gpg.yml` | perms (`0600` files, `0700` dir), `chown`, agent *config* only — no daemon restart (90-92) |
| `ssh` | `ssh.yml` | keypair via `community.crypto.openssh_keypair` (rsa 4096 + ed25519, no passphrase); macOS `~/.ssh/config` via `blockinfile` w/ marker → **fixes #45** (136-159) |
| `tpm` | `tpm.yml` | clone tpm, install plugins via detached-session workaround (175-188) |
| `prereqs` | `prereqs.yml` | Linux apt/pacman full developer list: `build-essential` + `zlib1g-dev` + `xdg-utils` + `bash-completion`; `apt update_cache=yes` always (full `apt upgrade` is gated to `dotfiles_state == 'latest'` in `upgrade.yml`) (203-211). Note: the minimal `curl git build-essential ca-certificates` needed to bootstrap brew itself lives in the residual `bootstrap.sh` (chicken-and-egg) — see below. |
| `rust` | `rust.yml` | rustup via `command` + `creates: ~/.cargo/bin/cargo` (213-223) |
| `mise` | `mise.yml` | install/self-update mise, `mise install node go bun ruby` (precompiled-fallback preserved), `corepack enable` (226-275) |
| `claude_opencode` | `tools_cli.yml` | `claude upgrade` / `opencode upgrade` if present (245-258) |
| `npm` | `npm.yml` | global node modules (`neovim eslint_d editorconfig`) guarded by `command -v eslint_d` (278-287) |
| `brew` | `brew.yml` | install Homebrew if missing; `homebrew_tap`; core `homebrew` formulae list from vars; tmux `--HEAD` + `homebrew` pinned state (issue #138 workaround preserved); Linux `gcc`; `git-delta` reinstall-on-mismatch guard (292-384) |
| `brew_casks` | `brew_casks.yml` | macOS-only formulae + casks; `brew bundle --global` when `~/.Brewfile` present (#152 hook) (387-411) |
| `nvim` | `nvim.yml` | vim-plug install + `nvim --headless +PlugInstall --sync +qall`; `pip3 install --user pynvim`; `gem install neovim`; `go install gopls` (414-428, 442-454) |
| `zoxide` | `zoxide.yml` | legacy `~/.z` → zoxide migration, idempotent (431-439) |
| `beads` | `beads.yml` | `bd bootstrap` / `bd dolt remote add` — pure commands (461-480) |
| `upgrade` | `upgrade.yml` | **Only included when `dotfiles_state == 'latest'`.** Owns the upgrade semantics for everything modules can express (`apt upgrade=yes`, `pacman -Syu`, `homebrew upgrade_all`, `homebrew_cask upgrade`, `pip/gem state=latest`, `mise upgrade --yes`) plus the command-based upgrades modules can't express: `rustup self-update && rustup update`, `nvim +PlugUpdate --sync`, TPM `update_plugins` (detached-session workaround), `npm install -g <pkgs>`, `claude upgrade`, `opencode upgrade`, `bd dolt pull`. Tagged `upgrade` so `--tags upgrade` runs only these. |

`tasks/main.yml` includes them in dependency order (prereqs → rust → mise → brew → nvim, etc.).

### Variables (`defaults/main.yml`)
- `dotfiles_state:` `present` (default — install-if-missing, fast/safe) | `latest` (also upgrade everything; triggers `tasks/upgrade.yml`).
- `dotfiles_brew_core:` list (the always-installed core formulae — pulled from the current `brew install` block).
- `dotfiles_brew_linux:` (`gcc`) and `dotfiles_brew_macos:` formulae/cask lists.
- `dotfiles_mise_tools:` defaults `{node, go, bun, ruby}`.
- `dotfiles_npm_globals:` `{neovim, eslint_d, editorconfig}`.
- `dotfiles_ssh_key_email:` `"tribou@users.noreply.github.com"`.
- `dotfiles_home:` `{{ ansible_env.HOME }}` (overridable — enables root-in-container testing).

### Profiles & #152 (orthogonal — NOT subsumed)
Core lists are role vars (overridable via `--extra-vars` / inventory). Optional tooling stays on #152's file-drop mechanism: `~/.Brewfile` (consumed by `brew bundle --global`) and `~/.config/mise/conf.d/*.toml` (auto-merged by `mise install`). The role runs `mise install` and `brew bundle --global` (when files present) and is profile-dumb beyond core. **#152 ships as-is and remains open** — orthogonal to this role.

### Platform handling
Standard Ansible conditionals, no custom fact-gathering:
- macOS: `when: ansible_system == 'Darwin'`
- Debian/Ubuntu apt: `when: ansible_os_family == 'Debian'`
- Arch pacman: `when: ansible_os_family == 'Archlinux'`

### Secrets & keys
- SSH keys: `community.crypto.openssh_keypair` (idempotent — generates only if absent; rsa 4096 + ed25519; no passphrase, matching current behavior).
- macOS `~/.ssh/config`: `blockinfile` with `# BEGIN dotfiles` / `# END dotfiles` marker (idempotent — fixes #45).
- GPG signing key: **manual**, out of scope (README already documents it).
- `~/.ssh/api_keys`: **role ignores entirely**. Missing-env-var warnings stay in `bash_profile` (existing behavior — e.g. `GIT_SIGNING_KEY` warns if unset).
- Vault: documented as a future option, not built now.

### Residual `bootstrap.sh` (~30 lines)
Three responsibilities:
1. **Self-locate / self-clone.** If invoked via `curl|bash` (not inside the repo), install minimal `curl git ca-certificates`, then `git clone` to `~/dev/dotfiles` and re-exec itself there.
2. **Linux brew-bootstrap prereqs** (chicken-and-egg): `curl git build-essential ca-certificates` (apt) or `curl git base-devel` (pacman) — brew's installer needs a C toolchain before it can build on Linux. (macOS needs nothing extra.)
3. **Install brew (if missing) → `brew install ansible` → `exec ansible-playbook playbook.yml`.**

On success, print: `open a new login shell (or: exec $SHELL -l) so mise/gpg-agent/brew/cargo PATH take effect`. (Note: this restart requirement is **not new** — the current bash bootstrap has the identical requirement, since its inline `eval`s also die with the subprocess.)

The session-daemon `eval`s `gpg-agent --daemon` and `mise activate` stay in `bash_profile`/`zshrc` startup — they already run on every login shell. `ssh-agent` is **not** wired into shell startup today (out of scope here — tracked in follow-up #155); a fresh login shell does not bring it up, but on macOS the keychain covers SSH auth and on Linux passphraseless keys work without it.

**Prereq ownership split** (avoids #48-style duplication while respecting chicken-and-egg):
- `bootstrap.sh` owns the *minimal* set brew needs: `curl git build-essential ca-certificates`.
- Role `prereqs` task owns the *full* developer apt list: adds `zlib1g-dev xdg-utils bash-completion` and runs `apt update_cache=yes` on every run (the full system `apt upgrade` is gated to `dotfiles_state == 'latest'`, in `upgrade.yml`).
- Overlap on `build-essential` is intentional and documented (both are idempotent no-ops after first run).

**New-machine runbook** (three entry styles):
- **curl one-liner** — `bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tribou/dotfiles/HEAD/bootstrap.sh)"` (self-clones to `~/dev/dotfiles`).
- **explicit** — `mkdir -p ~/dev && git clone https://github.com/tribou/dotfiles.git ~/dev/dotfiles && cd ~/dev/dotfiles && ./bootstrap.sh`.
- **ansible already present** (CI / containers / re-runs) — `cd ~/dev/dotfiles && ansible-playbook playbook.yml`, or once bootstrapped, just `just install` from the repo (supports `--tags ssh,links` subsets and `--check --diff`).

**Repo location convention:** checkout lives at `~/dev/dotfiles` (matches `bash_profile`'s hardcoded `DOTFILES`). The role symlinks from absolute `role_path`, so the checkout path is the single source of truth for all link targets.

## Non-goals
- Replacing the session-daemon `eval`s (physically impossible from a subprocess).
- Generating the GPG signing key (interactive, manual).
- Managing `~/.ssh/api_keys` or adopting Vault in this pass.
- Subsuming #152 (file-drop opt-in stays as #152 specifies).
- Changing the `lib/` shell libraries or the bats unit tests (they test shell functions, not bootstrap).
- Removing `bootstrap.sh` entirely (it stays as the thin brew+ansible bootstrapper).

## Testing
**Both** frameworks, by role:
- **Molecule** (`roles/dotfiles/molecule/`) — role-dev loop: `molecule converge` for fast iteration, `idempotence` phase auto-runs converge again and asserts `changed=0` (directly serves driver #1). Verifier reuses `goss.yaml` (no porting). `molecule create` uses a matching Ubuntu image.
- **Docker + goss + bats** — retained as CI integration gate (`just test`) and `just dev` interactive entrypoint. `Dockerfile` swaps `bootstrap.sh` → `ansible-playbook -i localhost, playbook.yml` against the container; `goss.yaml` contract unchanged; `tests/integration/*.bats` untouched.

## CI impact
- `Dockerfile`: replace the `bootstrap.sh` invocation with `ansible-playbook` (install ansible-core in the image, run against localhost). Layer caching still applies.
- `docker-compose.yml` / `just test`: unchanged contract, same goss+bats verification.
- Molecule: optional in CI initially; can be gated later as a separate job.

### Justfile targets (new)
- **`just install`** → `ansible-playbook playbook.yml` (default `dotfiles_state: present` — install/repair only). The daily-driver convenience wrapper for an already-bootstrapped machine. Note: `just`/`ansible` exist only after the first `./bootstrap.sh`, so the first-time entry remains `./bootstrap.sh` (or the curl one-liner); `just install` is for every re-run thereafter.
- **`just upgrade`** → `ansible-playbook playbook.yml -e dotfiles_state=latest --tags upgrade` (upgrade everything). Companion to `just install`.
- Both accept extra args forwarded to `ansible-playbook` (e.g. `just install --check --diff`, `just upgrade --tags brew`).

## Package updates (install vs upgrade)
The current `bootstrap.sh` only truly upgrades apt/pacman on re-run; Homebrew formulae, casks, mise tools, npm globals, nvim plugins, TPM, and rustup are install-only and silently skipped on re-run. The new structure makes updates first-class and explicit via a single variable:

- **`dotfiles_state: present`** (default) — every package module uses `state: present`; install-if-missing only. Re-running the playbook is fast and never triggers a surprise upgrade. This is the daily driver.
- **`dotfiles_state: latest`** — additionally includes `tasks/upgrade.yml` (tagged `upgrade`) which upgrades everything modules can express (`apt upgrade=yes`, `pacman -Syu`, `homebrew upgrade_all`, `homebrew_cask upgrade`, `pip/gem state=latest`, `mise upgrade --yes`) plus the command-based upgrades they can't (`rustup self-update && update`, `nvim +PlugUpdate --sync`, TPM `update_plugins`, `npm install -g <pkgs>`, `claude upgrade`, `opencode upgrade`, `bd dolt pull`).

Run modes:
- `./bootstrap.sh` (or curl one-liner) — **first-time entry** from scratch (installs brew + ansible, then execs the playbook). Required on a machine with no `just`/`ansible` yet.
- `just install` — re-run / repair on an already-bootstrapped machine (`ansible-playbook playbook.yml`, default `present`).
- `ansible-playbook playbook.yml -e dotfiles_state=latest --tags upgrade` — upgrade everything.
- `just upgrade` — convenience wrapper for the above.
- `--check --diff` works for previewing both modes (e.g. `just install --check --diff`).

Net: explicit intent, complete coverage (closes the gaps the current script silently skips), subset-able, and schedulable.

## Issues touched
- **Fixes #41** (rm -rf no backup → idempotent `file: link` + pre-link backup task).
- **Fixes #45** (macOS ssh config non-idempotent → `blockinfile` marker).
- **Fixes #48** (duplication across bootstrap.sh / Dockerfile / bootstrap-test.sh → single role is the source of *developer* state; the residual `bootstrap.sh` owns only the unavoidable brew-bootstrap prereqs (chicken-and-egg), documented as intentional overlap, not #48 duplication).
- **#152**: stays open, orthogonal (file-drop opt-in).
- **#138**: tmux `--HEAD` + pin workaround preserved as documented task.

## Open decisions
- None material. (Implementation details: whether to split the core brew list into a `vars/` file vs `defaults/` — defaults, for overridability; `--check`/`--diff` cleanliness across all tasks — goal; whether to ship a sample scheduled `just upgrade` wrapper — yes, documented.)

<details>
<summary>Brainstorm log</summary>

- [x] Q: Primary driver? A: All — reliability + maintainability + profiles.
- [x] Q: Layout/invocation? A: Role-in-repo + local playbook (`connection: local`); residual bootstrap.sh execs the playbook.
- [x] Q: Scope boundary? A: Aggressive — all but the ~3 session-daemon evals.
- [x] Q: Profiles & #152? A: Keep #152's file-drop mechanism; role stays profile-dumb beyond core vars. #152 orthogonal.
- [x] Q: Testing? A: Both — Molecule (dev loop + idempotence phase, goss verifier) + Docker/goss/bats (CI gate, `just dev`).
- [x] Q: Secrets & keys? A: Manage SSH keys via `openssh_keypair`; macOS ssh config via `blockinfile`; ignore `~/.ssh/api_keys`; GPG manual; missing-env warnings stay in bash_profile.
- [x] Q: New-machine runbook + bootstrap.sh content? A: 3 entry styles (curl one-liner / explicit clone / ansible-present); residual bootstrap.sh is ~30 lines (self-clone, Linux brew-bootstrap prereqs, brew+ansible, exec playbook); prereq ownership split documented.
- [x] Q: How are package updates handled vs installs? A: Variable-controlled — `dotfiles_state: present` (default, install-only) vs `latest` (also runs `tasks/upgrade.yml` covering apt/pacman/brew/casks/mise/npm/pip/gem/rustup/nvim/TPM/claude/opencode/beads). `just upgrade` convenience target. Current script only upgraded apt/pacman — this closes the coverage gaps.

</details>
title: feat(bootstrap): convert bootstrap.sh into an Ansible role
